title: Band-9 Samples: Did you go to secondary/high school near to where you lived? [Why/Why not?]
passage_html:
This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 10 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 1 Test 4 question:

“Did you go to secondary/high school near to where you lived? [Why/Why not?]”

Sample 1: Yes

Absolutely, my secondary education institution was just a stone’s throw away from my home. It was tremendously convenient because I could easily walk back and forth, which saved me a lot of time and hassle from commuting. The proximity also allowed me to have a bit more sleep in the morning, which was definitely a bonus.

Sample 2: Yes

Yes, my high school was in the same neighborhood where I resided. This was mainly due to the abundance of exceptional schools in my locality. I had the luxury to choose from a range of quality institutions, and I ended up choosing the one that was closest to my home.

Sample 3: Yes

I didn’t actually venture far for my high school education. My parents, who were often preoccupied with their busy careers, opted for a school that was nearby. For them, it was a pragmatic choice, not only providing convenience but also lessening the chance of any mishaps during the commute.

Sample 4: Yes

Yes, my secondary school was within walking distance from my home. The key reason was the sense of community that I felt there, largely due to the presence of my long-time pals from previous schooling years. This familiarity provided a sense of comfort and continuity in a period of significant change and growth.

Sample 5: No

Not at all. I was raised in a pastoral setting, and the nearest high school was quite a few miles away. We didn’t have a bus service, so my parents had to drive me every day. Despite the long distance, the drive was always scenic and peaceful, and it became a treasured part of my daily routine.

Sample 6: No

No, my secondary school was located quite far from where I lived. The reason behind this was simply the pursuit of quality education. The school in our vicinity wasn’t up to the mark, so my parents decided to enroll me in a more reputable institution, even though it meant a lengthy commute every day.

Sample 7: No

Actually, my high school was not only far from my home, it was in a completely different city. I attended a boarding school, so I resided in the school dormitory. The experience was exciting and taught me a great deal about independence and self-reliance at a young age.

Sample 8: No

I didn’t attend a high school in my local area. Instead, I was a student at an international school that was a fair distance from my home. This was largely due to the school’s unique bilingual program, which I was keen to be a part of. Despite the commute, the opportunity to become proficient in a second language was an invaluable experience.

Sample 9: Neither Near Nor Far

Strikingly, my high school was situated at a harmonious distance from my home – not too near, not too distant. This sweet spot was perfect for a leisurely morning stroll, allowing me to bask in the serene ambiance and converse with my friends who lived en route. It was a wonderful way to gear up for the day’s academic rigors.

Sample 10: Both

Interestingly, it was a mix of both. In the early years of my secondary education, I attended a school that was far from home, which was quite challenging due to the daily commute. However, a few years later, a new school opened closer to my neighborhood, and I transferred there, which made things significantly easier.
